Thanks for the ping - I started a repro and have a few early notes:

1) Payload: their sample shows batched embedding requests with ~5000 tokens per document and an inline reranker call in the same request. That gives very large content-length headers for some requests.
2) Timeouts: default routing/proxy timeout is 30s on their gateway; our embedding+reranker path can exceed that when reranker is invoked synchronously.
3) Auth header: some requests we saw in their snippets are missing the X-Redwood-Key and are going through the gateway without proper routing to our dedicated pool - those are getting routed to fallback endpoints resulting in 502s under load.

Immediate mitigation suggestions (will send a small PR/snippet):
- Increase client-side request timeout to 90s for long rerank + embedding runs OR split embedding batch and reranker into two sequential calls.
- Ensure SDK sets X-Redwood-Key header and Content-Length is accurate (when using chunked transfer, verify proxy supports it).
- Reduce per-request batch size from 32 -> 8 for embeddings and run top-k reranker separately.

I'm attaching a short SDK example that sets streaming and a longer timeout: redwood_sdk_snippet.py (snippet uses our python SDK to stream embeddings and call reranker as a separate step).

I can join the 10:30am PT slot tomorrow and will bring repro scripts and a load profile.

-Neha

Quick update from my repro run this morning: I reproduced the 502/504 when the gateway timed out on synchronous reranker calls. Attached is a trace for one failing request (request_trace.log) - the request id is rw-req-20260803-9a4f. Stack shows a gateway timeout while waiting for our reranker response; the backend did finish computation but the upstream gave up.

Two concrete fixes we can propose to FinLytics:
- Client change: split embedding and reranker into two calls (quickest to implement).
- Server-side: enable streaming responses and increase gateway timeout to 90s for the reranker route OR enable async reranker processing with callback/webhook.

Also flagging that their gateway strips the X-Redwood-Key for some large-chunked requests - recommend they set the header at the edge and verify passthrough to our proxies.

I can join the debug session tomorrow at 10:30am PT along with Neha.

-Ethan
